articles.title: 'When will you score runs?' Babar Azam's weaknesses exposed by ex-Pakistan player

He scored 45 against Sri Lanka and 34 against England, failing to build on important beginnings. Former cricketer Tanveer Ahmed has highlighted weaknesses in Babar's batting against spinners, incoming fast deliveries, and short balls. He emphasized the need for Babar to address these vulnerabilities to improve his performance.

articles.title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to support local artisans by prioritizing their products while shopping for festivals. He emphasized that doing so would strengthen the 'Vocal for Local' campaign and promote a self-reliant India. Modi highlighted successful local exports such as makhana and arhar dal to various international markets. Additionally, he discussed efforts aimed at reviving traditional skills and farming practices, including natural cotton cultivation.

articles.summary: Mary and Fred Holden's property settlement agreed to equal ownership of their Kentucky farm. Disagreements arose regarding when the farm should be listed for sale after two years. articles.title: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis expand $10M beach house after mudslides
articles.summary: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are planning a significant renovation of their Carpinteria beachfront property. The proposed changes include expanding the main residence and adding a swimming pool. They acquired the property in 2017 for $10.1 million and have seen its estimated value rise to about $17 million. The couple's plans involve the removal of a guest cottage to enhance the outdoor living space.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says US rules pushed China toward self-reliance
articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang pointed out that US export controls have significantly fueled China's semiconductor advancements. He remarked that these restrictions have compelled China to bolster its own chip production strengths. Huang also expressed strong faith in the US technology sector's resilience, despite heightened competition from China, and dismissed worries about an impending memory chip surplus, predicting ongoing demand for High Bandwidth Memory in the years ahead.

articles.title: IIT Madras graduates' hostel idea grows into over 1,500 foldable buildings
articles.summary: Modulus Housing, founded by IIT Madras graduates, focuses on manufacturing foldable buildings for quick assembly and transportation. Since 2018, it has provided over 1,500 modular structures across India and parts of Africa. The startup aims to improve access to essential infrastructure like schools and clinics, especially in rural areas. Recently, it raised ₹70 crore in funding to support further expansion and innovation.

articles.title: From unfinished books to 10-second reels: Is reading becoming lost art?
articles.summary: The growing preference for short-form digital content is raising concerns about children’s ability to engage with books and sustain attention. Educationists and experts examine declining reading habits, the role of examination-driven learning, and the impact of digital distractions. Drawing on research and Kerala’s library movement, the story explores ways to rebuild deep reading through schools, families and communities.

articles.title: Drone attack: Iran targets Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq
articles.summary: Iran's armed forces conducted a drone attack on the Komala group in Iraq's Kurdistan region. This operation reportedly caused significant damage and casualties to the group's infrastructure. Previous strikes on the Komala group have occurred since the regional conflict began in February. Iran accuses these opposition groups of receiving support from Israel, its longstanding adversary. The Kurdish opposition has denied allegations of receiving arms from Israel despite Iran's claims.

articles.title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 cr from investors

A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.

Residents reported that his spit, while chewing gutkha, made contact with the 11kV line. Locals expressed anger towards the electricity company for neglecting their complaints about unsafe wiring. articles.title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises

articles.title: From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at Asian Para Games

Their plan backfired when they were detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Both individuals used fake passports to evade law enforcement for several years. articles.summary: Himanshu Bhau, a notorious gangster from north India, was recently captured by the FBI in Las Vegas. After escaping juvenile detention in 2020, he maintained his criminal operations through illegal networks.

articles.title: Israel launches ‘limited counterterrorism’ op after 2 IDF troops killed in West Bank
articles.summary: In a post on X, the IDF said, "In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell, and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged." The storm brought heavy rain and strong winds, leading to widespread power outages affecting over 167,000 homes. Over 240 flights were canceled due to severe weather conditions impacting transport services. Schools and offices were closed for an extended period as a precautionary measure against the storm.

articles.title: 'We have to think about posting 350 first': Rauf on need for bigger totals

He stressed teamwork, middle-over breakthroughs and the need for bigger totals as ODI cricket becomes more aggressive. Rauf is also focusing on improving his pace and fitness, while backing Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to contribute runs in upcoming matches.

articles.title: Ryan Gosling and Eva Mendes bought retreat made from 200-year-old barns in 2014
articles.summary: In 2014, Ryan Gosling and Eva Mendes purchased a distinctive rustic estate in Carpinteria, California. This property, crafted by Joel Schumacher, is constructed from reclaimed wood of three 200-year-old barns. Designed for privacy and a serene connection to nature, it embodies American history, offering a tranquil retreat from Los Angeles. The couple cherishes their family life away from the spotlight, valuing their children and preserving the estate's unique features.

articles.title: Krasinski and Emily Blunt sell Brooklyn apartment for $6.5M, net $1.5M profit
articles.summary: John Krasinski and Emily Blunt have sold their nearly 1,600-square-foot apartment at The Standish in Brooklyn Heights for $6.5 million. A trust linked to the couple purchased the property for $5 million in January 2024. The off-market sale, completed in June 2026, represents a $1.5 million increase in value in just over two years.

articles.title: Dan vs Daniel: Trump admin sues to block Alaska result if GOP candidate loses race
articles.summary: The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Alaska on Thursday, argues that the state must protect the integrity of federal elections. It asks the court to block the certification of a Peltola victory if Daniel Sullivan, a candidate from the small fishing community of Petersburg, remains on the ballot. “The United States accordingly brings this lawsuit to protect the integrity of the 2026 Senate election in Alaska,” the lawsuit says.

articles.title: Video: Gunmen storm Jordan church during funeral, killing 7 and wounding 40
articles.summary: Jordan's government described the attackers as unknown assailants and said investigations were moving ahead at full speed. It did not immediately confirm whether any suspects had been arrested or killed. Footage aired by Jordanian state television showed two men appearing to carry pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and opened fire before all three ran towards the building.

articles.title: Tom Brady helped provide 750,000 meals to families in need in Tampa Bay

The contribution came shortly after the couple moved to Florida, where Brady began his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after 20 seasons with the New England Patriots. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.

articles.title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals

The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

articles.title: Need to unite against divisive forces, tackle new challenges: PM Modi

We must inspire citizens toward self-reliance, and we must connect every individual to vision of a developed India by 2047. For these objectives, we must become more proactive,” he said.

articles.title: Ukrainian soldier cuts off his own foot to survive, rescued by drone after 8 months
articles.summary: Kostiantyn Vlasenko, 49, had been stranded in a boiler room with severe injuries after a Russian drone strike. With no way to escape and little hope of being rescued, he made a desperate decision to amputate his remaining foot to survive. On October 4, a large drone lifted him into the air using a harness and carried him 15km to safety.

articles.title: Chloë Grace Moretz bought LA home at 19 for $3.4m, sold it for $5.65m

Studio City remains a popular area for high-profile buyers, including Olivia Wilde, who sold her property in December 2025.

articles.title: LA couple bought $925,000 farm, made barn a home, started cider business

Despite initial doubts, the farm has become a popular destination for families and children.

The estate has been purchased by David and Erika Sands, professional poker players, who now add it to their diverse real estate holdings across New York and California.

articles.title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
articles.summary: In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.

articles.title: Record growth, rising risks: What’s really driving India’s core industries? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.summary:
India’s core industrial sectors recorded a series-high growth rate of 7.9% in September, driven by strong performances in coal, electricity, steel and refinery products.

While the data points to a welcome industrial uptick, concerns remain about how sustainable the momentum will be. Much of the growth appears linked to temporary factors such as increased power demand during the heat wave and higher refining activity driven by imported oil.

With global crude prices rising, foreign exchange pressures mounting and infrastructure spending continuing to shoulder much of the growth burden, economists are questioning whether the current surge can be sustained in the coming months.

Anahat will now go head-to-head with Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam, reigniting their rivalry from the Asian Games final, solidifying her remarkable tournament journey in Redwood City.

articles.title: Facial laser session leaves woman with burns; consumer panel orders Rs 1.11 lakh payout
articles.summary: In an alarming incident at Berkowits Hair & Skin Clinic in Bengaluru, a woman suffered severe second-degree burns during a laser hair removal treatment. Despite her intense pain, the technician minimized her discomfort, labeling it as normal. Subsequent medical examinations validated her injuries. The district consumer commission held the clinic accountable for inadequate service and mandated compensation, including a refund and damages for her injuries and emotional distress.

articles.title: Paid Rs 1 lakh for gold chain, got nothing; jeweller ordered to pay Rs 1.3 lakh

Customer M R Chauhan made an advance payment for a gold chain that was never delivered. Despite repeated requests and a police complaint, the jeweller failed to return the money. The commission awarded compensation of Rs 20,000 for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 for litigation costs.

articles.title: US soldier killed at 17 in Korean War identified after 75 years, to be buried
articles.summary: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.

articles.title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
articles.summary: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO says Starlink is helping win customers; Musk responds
articles.summary: This week, United Airlines aims to have Starlink on more than half of its flights, looking to fully implement the service across its fleet by the end of the following year. CEO Scott Kirby believes this partnership offers a distinct edge in attracting new passengers, especially as rising fuel costs weigh on profits amidst ongoing geopolitical issues.

articles.title: Texas man, 86, spends 39 years building 62-foot boat; strangers step in
articles.summary: An 86-year-old man from Mineral Wells, Texas, has been building a 62-foot steel boat since 1987. After three visitors discovered his ambition, they launched a crowdfunding campaign to support the project. More than $41,000 has been raised towards completing the boat and moving it to a launch site. The remaining work on the vessel is expected to require about $50,000 in funding.

Viral fever, vomiting: How Praveen Kumar fought back to win Asian Para Games gold
articles.summary: Praveen Kumar won the men’s high jump T44/64 gold medal at the Asian Para Games in Japan. He accomplished this while dealing with a hip injury and battling fever, cold, and cough. Despite these challenges, he cleared 2.05m, setting a new Games record. His previous record was 1.95m in the T44 category. Praveen aims to defend his Paralympic title at the next Los Angeles Games.

articles.title: 'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'
articles.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited India to strengthen bilateral cooperation between India and Poland. He highlighted the absence of conflicts of interest and shared values between the two nations. Both leaders discussed expanding economic opportunities through the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. Tusk emphasized the positive economic developments achieved by Poland and India over the last 35 years.

articles.title: Exhibition row: Raihan recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down
articles.summary: Raihan Vadra's photography exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, allegedly faced turmoil at Bikaner House when management objected hours before its start, claiming venue policy violations. While Vadra proposed removing select images, the officials demanded the removal of all 70 photographs, including those depicting the Indian national flag. This sparked outrage among Congress members, igniting debates about censorship and the value of artistic freedom.

articles.title: Pala-era Vishnu sculpture sold for Rs 8.16 crore, over 9 times estimate
articles.summary: A blackstone sculpture of Vishnu, dating to the 11th or 12th century, sold for £635,000 at Christie’s auction. The sculpture was previously part of a Swiss collection and first sold in March 1973. Over the years, the artwork maintained its significance and desirability among collectors. In June 2026, it was auctioned again as part of a collection focusing on South Asian art.

articles.title: China's restored reefs hold 286 oysters per sq m; particles down 62%
articles.summary: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness.

articles.title: Georgia woman loses marijuana smoke case as court upholds pension fund immunity
articles.summary: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.

articles.title: Delhi-NCR pollution: How GRAP Stage 1 curbs can protect your heart and lungs
articles.summary: Delhi-NCR has launched GRAP Stage 1 to combat the rising air pollution levels and protect health standards. The initiative focuses on controlling dust, limiting specific fuel types, and tightening regulatory enforcement. Health experts stress the importance of immediate intervention to guard vulnerable populations against the health implications of poor air quality. articles.title: 'Vidhan Sabha uda diya': Bengaluru police arrest Bihar man over AI video

The video depicted a bomb blast at Vidhana Soudha, the Karnataka government's seat. The suspect, Hazrat Ali Shoiab, had been working as a daily-wage pipefitter in the city. Police discovered the footage during routine digital surveillance and tracked down the suspect's account. Investigations are ongoing to understand Shoiab's motives and identify any collaborators.

articles.title: Was Tiger Shroff the real target? | Pulse Maharashtra
articles.summary:
A celebrity shootout in Mumbai has sent shockwaves through the financial capital and has spread fear in the Hindi film industry. This wasn’t the first shootout in the city this year. And now, the industry is scared of the dark shadows of the past, when the underworld called the shots in Bollywood. And just like the past, this time too, the masterminds seem to be operating from foreign shores. But was Tiger Shroff the real target? Is this shootout related to incidents like the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique, the shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence and the reported threats to actors Ranveer Singh and Aamir Khan?

In this week’s Pulse Maharashtra with Vinaya Deshpande, we take you through what we know so far and what the unanswered questions are. And how this attack leads to an old fear in the heart of an industry which is one of India’s greatest soft powers in the world – Bollywood.

After spending seven days in jail, Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been released following an order by a Special Executive Magistrate court in Delhi.

The two leaders were detained after the October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar and had been held in judicial custody while police sought preventive action against them. The court eventually ordered their release after they submitted undertakings promising not to organise protests at Jantar Mantar while the site remains denotified and not to disturb public peace.

Students use it to mock suspected undercover officers’ attempts to infiltrate protest groups, though the allegation has not been confirmed.

articles.title: J&K MLA Shagun Parihar, Gujarat MP Hemang Joshi, UP's Nikhil Tiwari: Who are big names in BJP’s new youth wing team?

articles.title: Who is Jack Weis? Princeton PhD whose Nobel-cited research could not secure him a job after 2,300 applications
articles.summary: Jack Weis, a 30-year-old chemical engineering PhD from Princeton University, has applied for more than 2,300 jobs since graduating in 2024. Despite research cited by the 2024 Nobel Committee, he remains without stable employment.

articles.title: Meet Kerala woman who turned  ₹250 into mushroom business earning  ₹90 lakh annually: Here's how she did it
articles.summary: Shije started mushroom farming with an investment of  ₹250 in 2007. She and her husband, Thankachan, later launched Coon Fresh, expanding into mushroom cultivation, spawn sales, value-added products and training programmes.

articles.title: Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, Neha Bora Detention: Who are Special Executive Magistrates, why are they in news after SIR
articles.summary: The detention of CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, and a notice to AISA president Neha Bora, have spotlighted Special Executive Magistrates’ preventive powers amid SIR protests. The cases raise questions over procedural safeguards, peace bonds and the impact on personal liberty.

articles.title: Argentina eases drug import rules, creating new export avenues for India
articles.summary: The new framework dismantles long-standing regulatory barriers for Indian manufacturers, enabling a direct export of Indian medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), and medical equipment to Tucumán and other provinces.

articles.summary: Winter smog makes headlines, but toxic road silt never settles. With dust loads in Indian urban areas up to 30 times above many global cities, the country’s clean air fight faces an invisible wall. A ground report from the dustbowl of Gurugram.

articles.summary: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka withdrew their plea challenging custody extension in the Delhi High Court after the court asked them to await a lower court's review of their sureties. They were detained after allegedly climbing barricades at Jantar Mantar.

articles.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has invoked Stage-I of GRAP after Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) rose to 238 at 10 am on Wednesday, as per multiple reports.

articles.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. articles.summary: HDFC Bank is conducting an internal investigation into two senior executives for sharing confidential business information. The probe began after concerns were raised about potential information leaks to outsiders. As changes in leadership approach, the bank faces mounting challenges amid recent internal disagreements. Executive transitions include Anup Bagchi becoming the new chief executive later this month. The findings of this investigation will influence future decisions and strategies at the bank.

articles.title: Mirage 2000D crashes in France, one dead; search on for missing crew member
articles.summary: A French Mirage 2000D fighter jet crashed while returning to its air base after a night training mission. The aircraft crashed near Rogeville, approximately 18 km northwest of Nancy, during its final approach. One crew member has died, while another remains missing despite ongoing search efforts by the authorities. Investigations into the cause of the accident have been initiated by local authorities.

articles.title: 'Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres': What the viral message from French protests mean
‘Was it necessary?’ Anupam Kher slams BJP minister over Daler Mehndi row
articles.summary: Anupam Kher expressed his disappointment with BJP's Uttarkhand minister Subodh Uniyal's treatment of singer Daler Mehndi on stage. During a cultural event, Uniyal called out Mehndi for allegedly lip-syncing and questioned his sobriety. Kher emphasised the importance of addressing concerns privately to maintain dignity and respect. Singer Mika Singh defended Mehndi, citing his health issues and denying alcohol consumption allegations.

articles.title: US government fines Instacart $5 million over hiring practices
articles.summary: Instacart has been fined $5 million for allegedly discriminating against US-born workers in its hiring practices. The justice department accused Instacart of creating burdens for U.S. applicants during the Permanent Labor Certification process. A settlement has been reached, requiring Instacart to establish a fund for affected applicants and pay civil penalties. The company must also revise its employment policies and train staff on anti-discrimination laws.

articles.title: Missouri court overturns ruling giving couple ownership of neighbour's road
articles.summary: In a notable case from Missouri, a couple gained legal rights to their isolated property via their neighbor's land. Although the court initially granted them ownership of the access road, it later corrected this decision. Ultimately, they received a permanent easement, illustrating the difference between property rights and ownership. The couple can access their property while the neighbor retains the land under the road.

articles.title: Meloni toughens Italy protest laws: Teen detentions, parental liability, 5-year jail
articles.summary: In response to recent disturbances, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has introduced stringent security measures aimed at curbing protest-related violence. These measures entail prison sentences, fines, and even financial repercussions for parents of minors who participate in illegal protests. Authorities now have increased powers to detain youths perceived as threats, irrespective of actual criminal acts.

articles.title: Crude could hit $140 in early 2027 if Gulf supply disruptions persist: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: Commodity prices are expected to experience volatility due to geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions. Energy prices may rise sharply if Middle Eastern supplies remain constrained or degrade further. Agricultural markets could face pressure from various conflicts and potential weather disruptions linked to El Niño. Goldman Sachs anticipates significant price increases for copper and gold by 2027, driven by demand trends.

articles.title: 'I try to emulate his technique': Bavuma reveals Sachin Tendulkar influence
articles.summary: Temba Bavuma has hailed the influence of batting icon Sachin Tendulkar on his batting technique after notching up a personal best of 179 runs. He emphasized the significance of movement and keeping the bat close to the body. Satisfied with his innings, especially after a rough patch, Bavuma also credited Marco Jansen and Simon Harmer for their support, urging bowlers to elevate their game as well.

articles.title: Margot Robbie's $950,000 Hollywood bungalow later sold for about $1.2m
articles.summary: In February 2018, Margot Robbie bought a charming 945-square-foot bungalow in Hollywood Heights for $950,000. After giving it a stylish makeover, she rented it out at various rates. She eventually sold the property in 2021 for around $1.2 million, marking a profitable investment. This venture underscores the appeal of smaller homes in attractive neighborhoods, complementing her extensive property collection across Los Angeles and Australia.

articles.title: Assam man earned Rs 6 a day; his farm now turns over up to Rs 80 lakh a year
articles.summary: Tileswar Handique's remarkable journey began at the age of 15, working as a daily-wage labourer in Assam. A pivotal moment during a banana sale prompted him to shift towards agriculture, where he now enjoys a successful farm generating up to Rs 80 lakh a year. Passionate about sustainability, Handique practices natural farming and nurtures traditional crops while empowering others through training sessions and exhibitions, paving the way for community growth.

articles.title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan marks 10 years in Hawaii, donates $1.48m to hospital
articles.summary: In a remarkable gesture of generosity, Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have contributed $1.48 million to the Wilcox Medical Center in Kauaʻi. This donation will be utilized to purchase a mobile MRI unit and a 3D mammography machine, reinforcing their decade-long commitment to enhancing healthcare in the community. Overall, their philanthropy has exceeded $4 million, fundamentally improving access to vital medical resources for local residents.

articles.title: Woman who revived boyfriend twice after lightning strike to get bravery award
articles.summary: During a hiking trip, Eva Broderick's quick thinking saved her boyfriend Nick's life after they were both struck by lightning. Stranded in an isolated area, they faced delays as rescuers searched for them without precise location data. After their recovery, Nick's heartfelt proposal led to their wedding nearly a year later in August. Eva's heroic actions highlight the life-saving potential of CPR knowledge in unpredictable outdoor situations.

articles.title: ‘Term UN experts is oxymoron’: Rubio calls anti-EC protests ‘domestic political matter’
How Neeraj Chopra and wife Himani are building a sports business for a lasting legacy
articles.summary: Neeraj Chopra, along with his wife Himani Mor, has launched a sports management company named Vel Sports. This new venture aims to prioritise athletes' needs and enhance their performance while managing commercial commitments. The couple’s shared experiences in elite sports inform their approach to athlete representation and support. Additionally, the Neeraj Chopra Foundation focuses on developing emerging talent and improving coaching standards in India.

articles.title: ‘Dead letter box’, Rs 80,000: How 2 women supplied weapons to Tiger Shroff’s shooters
articles.summary: Investigators have reportedly found a weapons supply network in connection with the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's car. Two accused allegedly traveled to Amritsar to collect firearms, sourced through a dead letter box. Anil Pandit is believed to have orchestrated these operations while compensating the accused for their involvement. The accused initially intended to target a different Bollywood celebrity before shifting to Shroff.

Missouri court dismisses widow's appeal in $220,000 trust row as too late
articles.summary: Diane Longsdon encounters a significant legal hurdle as an appeals court dismisses her bid to contest a $220,000 repayment order. The issue originated from modifications to a family trust created by Violet M. Steinert and her spouse in 1994. Although Longsdon initially received money from these alterations, a court later upheld the original trust's validity.

articles.title: Ishan Kishan on the verge of three major T20 records as India take on New Zealand
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan is gearing up for an exciting five-match T20I series against New Zealand, where he stands merely seven runs shy of breaking Suryakumar Yadav's impressive record for the most T20I runs within a year. With additional matches against Sri Lanka looming ahead, Kishan is poised to chase more milestones, aiming to become the first Indian cricketer to amass 2,000 T20 runs in a single calendar year.

articles.title: Man repeatedly sent unsuitable matrimony profiles; commission orders Rs 37,000 relief
articles.summary: A consumer commission in Kerala has criticized a matrimonial agency for not fulfilling its service promises. The agency engaged in unfair trade practices, deceiving clients into buying pricier packages. In response to a complaint by Akhil Vinod, the commission mandated a refund and additional compensation. They highlighted the importance of matrimonial agencies transparently detailing their services to prevent consumer deception.

articles.title: England rugby legend Dallaglio's 2003 World Cup medal sold for £54,000
articles.summary: An exciting auction spotlighted an array of sports memorabilia, notably sounding the sale of Lawrence Dallaglio's silver-gilt medal from the 2003 Rugby World Cup, fetching £54,000. Collectors clamored for not only this remarkable piece but also his British and Irish Lions cap. Further captivating bids were made on football items, including Eric Cantona's iconic shorts and a BBC World Cup table, showcasing the rising allure of sports collectibles.

articles.title: Visually impaired Hyderabad student invents talking medicine box, wins award
articles.summary: A simple question about how visually impaired people identify their medicines led Rehan Raza to develop a device that speaks out a tablet’s name, dosage and timing, earning his project national recognition.

articles.title: Australian MP Helen Haines has both legs amputated after car attack
articles.summary: Helen Haines, an Australian federal lawmaker, is in critical condition following a violent car incident. Both of her legs were amputated due to severe injuries sustained during the attack. The accused driver, Brendan Nugent, has been charged but has not yet entered a plea. This incident has raised concerns about the safety of elected officials in Australia, prompting discussions on security measures.

articles.title: Reliance Industries stock surges 2% as Jio IPO gets fully subscribed in 100 minutes
articles.summary: the National Stock Exchange, RIL shares advanced as much as 1.96 per cent to Rs 1,225.60 apiece. During intraday trading, the stock had climbed 2.68 per cent to touch a high of Rs 1,234.30. Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213-crore IPO has been priced in the range of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share.

articles.title: India moves to develop its first indigenous aviation gun for Prachand, Rudra helicopters
articles.summary: India's Defence Research and Development Organisation has shortlisted two domestic firms for developing an indigenous 20mm aviation gun. This initiative aims to increase indigenous content in the Light Combat Helicopter Prachand and Rudra helicopters. The development is expected to take around two years before production orders are distributed based on cost calculations. Additionally, efforts are ongoing to indigenise the helicopters' other weapon systems, including anti-tank guided missiles.

articles.title: Men’s jewellery beyond ceremonial gold chain & ring: Luxury’s untapped frontier
articles.summary: Men's jewellery is undergoing a transformation, transcending traditional designs and momentary trends as it emphasizes individual style and self-expression. The industry is adapting, introducing pieces that prioritize comfort and men’s unique tastes. With lab-grown diamonds enhancing accessibility, men can curate their collections over time. This shift marks a vital change where personal choice takes precedence over cultural norms, paving the way for luxury jewellery that embodies everyday significance.

articles.title: SBI data leak: Nearly 4,000 customer records found on dark web; what we know so far
articles.summary: The State Bank of India has confirmed that 3,897 customer records may have been compromised and found on the dark web. Following alerts from cybersecurity agencies, an initial investigation revealed that sensitive personal data such as mobile numbers and loan details were involved. SBI has initiated its cyber incident response plan and is actively looking into the breach's validity and origins.

articles.title: 'Damning photos': Oppn targets Hardeep Puri's 'private meeting' pic with Epstein
articles.summary: Leaders from Congress, TMC, and NCP have voiced strong disapproval of Hardeep Singh Puri for his dealings with Jeffrey Epstein. Puri has contended that his interactions came during a professional delegation after his ambassadorial tenure. Critics are calling for clarification about the substance of these encounters, emphasizing their concerns over the ramifications of Puri's associations with someone linked to serious criminal charges.

Avengers Assemble: From Captain America to Spider-Man, superheroes run wild in France
articles.summary: Recent protests in France saw participants dressed as superheroes like Captain America, Batman, and Spider-Man. While demonstrations began with student grievances, they broadened to include various groups united against rising living costs. In cities like Marseille and Paris, clashes with police erupted, where costumed figures captured attention amid the unrest. Additionally, historical figures such as Napoleon were also spotted among demonstrators.

articles.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann 'detained for 3 hours' at Delhi airport, fined Rs 50k
articles.summary: Aam Aadmi Party has alleged that Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was detained at Delhi airport recently. He was held for three hours and subsequently issued a challan of Rs 50,000. AAP officials claim this incident reflects a deliberate attempt to humiliate Mann by the BJP-led central government. The party asserts that this move undermines the dignity of Punjab.

‘Bhuvi will love these conditions’: Why NZ fear India’s returning ‘Swing King’
articles.summary: New Zealand's captain, Mitchell Santner, recognises Bhuvneshwar Kumar as a significant threat for the team. With his skill to swing the ball and vast experience, he poses a unique challenge, especially in New Zealand conditions. Having not played T20I cricket for nearly four years, his return brings much-needed strength to India's bowling.

articles.title: 'Pay community dividend': Trump's message to companies building massive data centres
articles.summary: Donald Trump has proposed that large data centres should generate their own electricity and sell surplus power. He emphasized the potential for lower electricity prices through this model for local communities and the grid. Companies are encouraged to provide financial benefits to increase acceptance of data centre projects. Trump has linked the expansion of these centres to competition with China in artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Wisconsin farmer fights $900m power line that could cross 120 acres of farm
articles.summary: In western Wisconsin, rural landowners are rallying against the MariBell Transmission Project due to its anticipated negative impact on their land. The proposed route threatens family farms, with fears of diminished usable land, decreased property values, and potential health concerns. As the regulatory process moves forward, legal actions have emerged against the developers, accompanied by vigorous public protests, showcasing the strong resistance from the community of farmers and residents.

articles.title: Kaley Cuoco's 40-acre California ranch is now a refuge for rescued animals
articles.summary: In 2017, The Big Bang Theorystar Kaley Cuoco purchased a 40-acre ranch in California for $4.99 million. Nine years later, the property has become a refuge for rescued horses, cows, goats, pigs, donkeys and birds. Cuoco has transformed the ranch into a home for animals, including older ones rescued from difficult conditions, while also making it an important part of her family life.

articles.title: Chance the Rapper's charity backed Chicago youth therapy with $100,000 grant
articles.summary: Chance the Rapper's philanthropic venture, SocialWorks, has dedicated itself to bolstering mental health support for Chicago’s youth. By funding Under the Rainbow, a therapy initiative aimed at trauma-affected young individuals, SocialWorks strives to enhance access to emotional aid and nurture safe healing spaces. This initiative is part of a broader mission to uplift community well-being and empower the next generation by tackling pressing mental health issues.

articles.title: The Mecca Pact names no enemy, but why is it raising concerns in India?
articles.summary: Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defense agreement on August 7, which raises security concerns for India. The agreement includes a NATO-style Article 5, meaning an attack on one is an attack on all. India is analyzing the implications of this alliance, especially due to its complex relations with Turkey and Saudi Arabia. Pakistan has deployed significant military resources to Saudi Arabia amidst ongoing regional tensions with Iran.

articles.title: 'We have plans for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi': Santner sends warning to India
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could be a tough batter to stop if he gets a chance in India's playing XI for the five-match T20I series. articles.title: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of hypocrisy over RSS remarks on women’s rights

They accused him of hypocrisy regarding women's respect based on his behavior towards women. BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan emphasized Gandhi's failure to address allegations against a Congress MP involved in harassment. Additionally, BJP MLA Ram Kadam challenged Gandhi's understanding of the RSS's women's wing.

articles.title: Taxman caps SBI retiree’s leave exemption at Rs 3 lakh; but ITAT grants full relief
articles.summary: Under income tax law, SBI staff are treated as non-government employees and, therefore, can claim leave encashment exemption subject to the applicable limit. articles.title: Influencer with 1.3 million followers dies by suicide in Chennai

His father accused another influencer, Jason Samuel, of causing severe mental distress through defamatory posts. Harish's online channels were reported and blocked multiple times, contributing to his emotional turmoil. Before his death, he recorded a video blaming Samuel for his situation. Police have registered a case and are investigating the claims made by both parties.
